title: Netanyahu denies report Trump blocked Iran strike
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday denied a Financial Times report that the Jewish state recently planned to attack Iran but was stopped by U.S. President Donald Trump. "This report is not true," Netanyahu said in an interview with Israel National News . The premier declined to elaborate further. The British newspaper on Wednesday cited three sources familiar with the plans as saying that the Israel Defense Forces had prepared for a days-long campaign of intensive strikes on Iranian targets during the weekend of Oct. 10. The planned operation reportedly included attacks on nuclear facilities, power plants and other infrastructure. According to the newspaper, the offensive did not go ahead because Trump opposed resuming hostilities before the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3. One source said Israel and the United States could still resume military operations in the coming weeks. In the INN interview, Netanyahu said he had instructed the IDF and the Mossad to bring down the Iranian regime. He said Iran and its "axis of evil" were "weaker than ever." He warned that Tehran is still working to obtain nuclear weapons despite the damage done to its nuclear sites.

description: U.K. Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis said on Wednesday that he hoped a new report detailing the rise of antisemitism in English educational institutions would "prove to be a significant step towards protecting Jewish pupils." The report, overseen by Sir David Bell, a former schools inspector, was released on Wednesday. It offers 27 recommendations to combat the phenomenon. "Antisemitism is the ultimate othering, often driven by ignorance, which is the enemy of the cohesive and empathetic society we wish to build for all citizens," Mirvis posted to X. "With this in mind, the Bell Review reveals a deeply troubling level of antisemitism in our schools and colleges and is a painful indication of how far the situation has deteriorated. I commend Sir David Bell for his important work," he said. "I also welcome the government’s decision to adopt all 27 of its recommendations and look forward to seeing them implemented in full."

Biden "slapped an embargo on us in the middle of a war," Netanyahu said. "And what did he say? He said, 'What are you going to fight with?'" "I said, 'We'll fight with our fingernails if we have to.' Netanyahu said the Jewish state should be worried if current "trends in the United States" capture the White House in two years. No Israeli security personnel were injured. The suspects were handed over to the Shin Bet for further questioning. The announcement came shortly after the police denied reports circulating on social media of a security incident near Teddy Stadium in southwestern Jerusalem. Police stressed there was "no unusual security incident" in the area and that the soccer match between Beitar Jerusalem and Maccabi Tel Aviv was continuing as usual. "We call on the public to rely on and heed official announcements from the Israel Police and the security forces, and to act responsibly when spreading information," the statement added. title: French Jewish leader: Curfews have yet to restore confidence
description: France’s newly announced security measures have yet to restore confidence in authorities’ ability to contain rioting, a leader of the French Jewish community told JNS on Tuesday. “This week will be a very important week in order to know if the state takes back the power or not,” said Robert Ejnes, executive director of CRIF (Conseil Représentatif des Institutions Juives de France), the umbrella organization representing French-Jewish institutions. Asked whether he had confidence that authorities would be able to restore order in the face of the mass rioting, he said: “Not yet. We need to wait.” Bruno Benjamin, the head of the CRIF branch of Marseille-Provence this week urged French President Emmanuel Macron to declare a national state of emergency. On Monday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced “partial” and “localized” curfews following the weekend’s riots, in which at least 150 police officers were injured, according to Le Monde . The riots, which began last month ostensibly over poor conditions in French schools, have descended into violence against police, arson and vandalism, as well as widespread looting. Palestinian flags, in addition to Moroccan and Algerians ones, waved at protests have highlighted the role of immigrants from Muslim countries in the rioting. Benjamin accused the far-left France Unbowed party, or LFI, of orchestrating the riots, with help from people "who live in France, but hate France." Ejness said that the justice system’s handling of about 1,800 people who’d been arrested during the rioting in recent days was a major test for the state’s resolve to end the escalation. “We’re very eager to know now what will happen” to those arrested, he said, to establish “if the rule of law will prevail in France or whether these same people will be out by the next riot.” Lecornu appeared “determined” to stop the violence, Ejnes said, but added that a partial curfew offered only a temporary response. Ejnes also challenged claims circulating in Israel and on Jewish social media that rioters were systematically targeting Jewish businesses. Some Jewish-owned stores had suffered attacks, he said, but that alone did not establish an antisemitic motive. On Saturday night, a synagogue in the 19h Arrondissement of Paris was ransacked in an incident that Ejnes said did not feature any evidence of an antisemitic attack, and which seemed to suggest a robbery. Ejnes commented on a report Sunday by journalist Paul Amar of the Cnews television channel about a street in Marseille where only Jewish-owned stores hed been targeted. Ejnes said that he was aware of the report, but that it was not indicative of a phenomenon in which Jews are specifically targeted. Benjamin in Marseille told JNS the information reported by Cnews was “false.” The French-Jewish community’s security organization, SPCJ (Le Service de protection de la communauté juive ) , issued a statement saying it had no evidence that businesses had been attacked specifically because their owners were Jewish, Ejnes noted. That assessment offered no guarantee against future antisemitic attacks, Ejnes added. “We cannot be reassured that things will go well. We have to be realistic,” he said. “We have to raise the level of defense of the Jewish community, which is what we’re doing.”

title: Vance 'not getting involved in the Israeli elections' after Trump endorses Netanyahu
description: U.S. Vice President JD Vance said on Monday that he would be staying out of foreign elections when asked whether he would endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The question came a day after President Donald Trump gave Netanyahu his "complete and total endorsement" ahead of Israel's Oct. 27 Knesset elections. Vance told Mark Halperin's podcast, "2WAY Tonight," that Trump has "the most effective endorsement in American or international political history." In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump praised Netanyahu's leadership against Iran. "This is the kind of partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel," Trump wrote, calling Netanyahu "strong, brave, and brilliant." Vance said he only endorses "American candidates." He added, "that's what I'm focused on" as the U.S. midterm elections approach. Asked directly whether he backed Netanyahu, Vance said, "I'm not anti-endorsing him; I'm not pro-endorsing him." In April, Vance made a two-day campaign visit to Hungary to back the reelection bid of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. Five days later, Orbán was voted out of office in a landslide victory for the opposition Tisza party. At an Orbán rally during the visit, Vance told voters he was "not telling you exactly who to vote for," before urging them to "stand with Viktor Orbán, because he stands for you." title: Narratives blaming Jews for French riots sweep X, report finds

Over a two-day period, the ARC documented 1,384 such posts from 816 unique accounts. The most common terminology variants included: Jewish elite orchestration, Israel/Mossad orchestration, Zionist manipulation, “Pro-Israel accounts are behind it,” Kalergi/Great Replacement, Rothschild/ZOG/money, and “Who benefits,” said CAM, a global coalition of interfaith organizations. The same pattern on X followed when tens of thousands of migrants crossed into Ceuta, Spain, on July 30, 2026, according to CAM. Posts from 119 influencer accounts recast the border crisis as a Jewish plot, reaching an estimated 103 million people in 72 hours, ARC has found. When terrorists tried to hijack FlyDubai flight FZ1073 to Tel Aviv on Sept. 30, 2026, the first post blaming Israel appeared 67 minutes after the distress signal, CAM continued. The ARC collected 18,381 posts from X using 25 search queries in 7 languages. Any post linking the unrest in France to Jews, Israel, Zionists, or the Mossad was counted as antisemitic, according to CAM. Researchers read all 4,922 candidate text groups by hand and reviewed the 100 most-viewed posts individually.
